day_shape: 60 items: Strait of Hormuz remains closed with $100 oil, Jerusalem Post reports Trump nearing decision on major Iran combat operation, House passes war powers resolution 214-208, Iraqi PM Zaidi in Tehran, reported explosions in Kuwait and Qeshm.

threads.label: US-Iran military escalation decision point
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Trump is close to deciding on a new major combat operation against Iran, while Rubio said the price for Iran's escalation would rise nightly. IRIB claimed the House passed a war powers resolution limiting military action 214-208, with four Republicans joining Democrats.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz closure and oil at $100
threads.summary: IRIB said the IRGC Navy confirmed the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked with ships awaiting passage permits, and Parliament Speaker tweeted after oil hit $100. Khamenei adviser Mokhber claimed the $100 price reflects transport disruption not production, and Jerusalem Post reported Houthi threats to Bab el-Mandeb.

threads.label: Reported strikes and explosions across Gulf
threads.summary: IRIB reported explosions in Kuwait and the Qeshm Strait, while the Jerusalem Post cited an IRGC claim of damaging US equipment, drones and a Patriot system at Kuwait bases. Jerusalem Post also reported Iranian threats over Gulf infrastructure including Amazon systems in Bahrain and Kuwaiti utilities.

threads.label: Regional diplomacy: Iraq, Pakistan, Gulf statement
threads.summary: Iraqi PM Zaidi arrived in Tehran to meet Pezeshkian, signing joint MOUs at Saadabad Palace, while Pakistan's foreign minister said Islamabad is facilitating US-Iran dialogue. Defa Press denounced a joint Gulf states and Jordan statement accusing Iran of violating the UN Charter over strikes on US bases.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressure: protests, wages, France
threads.summary: Iran International reported protester Ahad Shokouhian received three death sentences over January demonstrations and warned unpaid workers have two months of resilience left. France said two diplomats detained in Tehran for nearly four hours, one allegedly beaten, have returned home.

events.title_en: End of working hours, start of energy waste
events.summary_en: End of working hours, start of energy waste. Under a cabinet resolution, government departments and institutions are obliged to reduce their electricity consumption during non-working hours by 70 per cent compared to consumption on the same day. Some departments have not yet taken this resolution seriously, and this matter has caused electricity supplies to be cut in Tehran Province government buildings since the start of summer until now.

events.title_en: Anti-Iran statement by Persian Gulf states and Jordan
events.summary_en: Anti-Iran statement by Persian Gulf states and Jordan. In a joint statement, Persian Gulf states and Jordan have made accusations against Iran without condemning American and Zionist regime aggression. In the statement, Iran's attack on American bases in the region is described as an 'open violation and breach of the UN Charter and international law'. These countries have also said: 'We preserve the right to lawful self-defence individually or collectively and will take any legal measures we deem necessary to protect our sovereignty.'

events.title: A Hamas terrorist who invaded Israel during the October 7 onslaught and two other members of the terror group were killed in an Israeli strike in the Gaza Strip this week, the IDF and Shin Bet announce. The strike on Tuesday in the Strip's north targeted Abdallah Jahja, a member of Hamas's naval force. The IDF says that Jahja invaded Israel on October 7 and during the war and recently advanced attacks "in the maritime domain" against Israeli troops and civilians. Alongside Jahja, the army says that two other Hamas operatives were killed in the strike: Mohammed Al-Hawari and Sabhi Saqallah, both members of the Zeitoun Battalion.
events.summary:

events.title: Rushdie attacker contacted person in Iran before attack, US prosecutors say
events.summary: US federal prosecutors said the man convicted of stabbing author Salman Rushdie contacted a person in Iran before the 2022 attack to confirm that the fatwa calling for Rushdie's death remained valid, the New York Times reported, as his federal terrorism trial opened on Wednesday.
